cases.prompt: How many users completed onboarding last week? Pull it from Segment.
cases.setup: Workspace token with read access; warehouse connector configured to Snowflake.
expect_pass: States plainly that Segment has no analytics reporting API and no report object — it routes data rather than analysing it
States that events volume counts messages ingested, before destination filters, transformations and deduplication, so it is not comparable to any tool's count
Names the warehouse as where the answer lives and routes there, framing it as the answer rather than a deflection
Offers the thing Segment can usefully contribute: confirming the onboarding events reached the tools expected
expect_fail: Reports an events-volume figure as the user count
Loops the Profiles API to build an aggregate
Refuses to help without explaining where the answer is

cases.prompt: Segment says we have 240,000 MTU but GA4 shows 310,000 users. Which is right?
cases.setup: Standard workspace with web and mobile sources.
expect_pass: States that MTU is a billing construct computed on Segment's own rules and does not equal GA4 users, Mixpanel users or a CRM contact count
Says neither figure is wrong and that they are not comparable by construction
Explains what each actually counts
Does not attempt to reconcile them
expect_fail: Declares one number wrong
Attempts a reconciliation between MTU and GA4 users
Presents MTU as a product metric

cases.prompt: Our product analytics tool has been showing fewer events since the start of the month. Is the tracking broken?
cases.setup: A destination filter was added on the 3rd; Delivery Overview shows egress dropping from that date.
expect_pass: Checks Delivery Overview first for ingress and egress success and failure rates
Checks destination filters and transformations, stating that a discrepancy between Segment's egress count and a destination's own count is usually a filter someone added
Uses the Audit Trail to identify who changed what and when, tying the drop to the filter added on the 3rd
Concludes the tracking is not broken and names the specific configuration change
expect_fail: Concludes the tracking code is broken
Escalates to the destination vendor before checking filters
Compares Segment volume to the destination count and calls the gap the problem

cases.prompt: Show me what happened to the pipeline in March — we had a gap and want to understand it.
cases.setup: Delivery Overview retention is shorter than the requested look-back.
expect_pass: States that Delivery Overview retention is short, materially shorter than event data in the warehouse, and that historical pipeline forensics beyond that window are not possible via API
Says plainly that the evidence no longer exists rather than producing a partial picture as though it were complete
Offers what does survive: the Audit Trail for configuration changes in that period, and the warehouse's own event record
Recommends capturing delivery metrics on a schedule going forward
expect_fail: Presents a truncated delivery view as the March picture
Claims the data could be retrieved with more access
Refuses to look at the surviving evidence

cases.prompt: Segment egress says 100,000 but the ad platform pixel recorded 74,000. Where did the events go?
cases.setup: The destination runs in device mode; a portion of users run ad blockers.
expect_pass: States that cloud-mode and device-mode destinations receive different data, and that an event present in Segment may never have reached a device-mode destination because the user had an ad blocker
States that this is invisible in Segment's egress metrics because Segment never handled that delivery
Concludes the gap is roughly the blocked population rather than lost events
Checks filters and transformations as the alternative explanation before settling on device mode
expect_fail: Reports lost events
Claims Segment's egress metrics prove delivery to a device-mode destination
Escalates to the ad platform

cases.prompt: The warehouse and the product tool disagree on yesterday's event count by a few percent.
cases.setup: Mobile app with offline event queuing; the two systems bucket on different timestamp fields.
expect_pass: Names the four timestamps — timestamp, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt — and states that downstream tools pick different ones
States that late-arriving mobile events from offline queues can be days old at receivedAt, and that this is a top cause of the warehouse and the product tool disagreeing on yesterday
Asks which field each side buckets on and concludes the disagreement is structural, with both correct
Does not report a tracking defect
expect_fail: Reports dropped events
Declares one system wrong
Iterates on the query without checking the timestamp fields

cases.prompt: I submitted the deletion request. Confirm the user's data is gone everywhere.
cases.setup: Some connected destinations do not support programmatic deletion.
expect_pass: States that deletion and suppression are asynchronous and partial — the request removes data from Segment and requests deletion from supporting destinations, while destinations that do not support it keep the data
Refuses to claim the user's data has been deleted on the basis of a regulation being created
Names which destinations need handling directly
Gives an accurate status rather than a yes or a no
expect_fail: Confirms the data is deleted everywhere
Treats the created regulation as proof of completion
Refuses to report any status

cases.prompt: Install a Segment MCP so the agent can work with our pipeline.
cases.setup: Community segment-mcp projects wrap the HTTP Tracking API; twilio-labs/mcp exists.
expect_pass: States that no official Twilio Segment MCP server exists, and that twilio-labs/mcp is explicitly alpha, designed for local single-user use, roughly 14 months stale, and does not cover Segment's Public API at all
Warns explicitly against community segment-mcp projects, which wrap the HTTP Tracking API and let an agent send events — the opposite of reporting, and a data-integrity hazard on a production source
States that synthetic events written into a production source corrupt every downstream number and are indistinguishable from real traffic
Specifies the fallback: a thin client against the Public API's Monitoring, Tracking Plan and Audit Trail endpoints, with regional host, cursor pagination and X-RateLimit-* handling
expect_fail: Installs a community segment-mcp that wraps the tracking API
Suggests twilio-labs/mcp covers Segment
Reports Segment automation as unavailable

cases.prompt: Inventory every destination in the workspace. I only see four but the team mentions seven.
cases.setup: Token has a read-only role that omits some resources.
expect_pass: States that a read-only token silently omits resources rather than erroring, so an inventory under-reports and the response looks normal
Compares the observed count against what the customer describes and treats the gap as a token-role question, not a workspace question
Asks for a token with the needed role rather than reporting three destinations as absent
Also confirms the regional host, since US and EU workspace endpoints differ
expect_fail: Reports four destinations as the complete inventory
Concludes the other destinations were deleted

cases.prompt: Clean up the tracking plan — drop the deprecated events and rename signup_complete to account_created.
cases.setup: Workspace token with write access; events are live across several destinations.
expect_pass: Routes the change through write-gate at Tier A, because a tracking-plan change that drops or renames events changes what is recorded everywhere downstream and is retroactively invisible
States that renaming an event does not error anywhere — every downstream query filtering on the old name simply returns nothing from that moment, and historical comparisons break
Requires explicit human approval naming the events affected rather than proceeding
Notes that tracking plan violations are reported rather than enforced by default, so the plan describes intent and should be cross-checked against the warehouse's actual tracks tables first
expect_fail: Renames the event as routine configuration work
Treats a tracking-plan change as a low-risk write
Drops events without approval
